data.title: We Think U10's (EPA:ALU10) Solid Earnings Are Understated
data.description:
U10 Corp (EPA:ALU10) announced a healthy earnings result recently, and the market rewarded it with a strong uplift in the stock price. Looking deeper at the numbers, we found several encouraging factors beyond the headline profit numbers.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Zooming In On U10's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

U10 has an accrual ratio of -0.21 for the year to June 2026. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of €14m, well over the €2.40m it reported in profit. Notably, U10 had negative free cash flow last year, so the €14m it produced this year was a welcome improvement.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On U10's Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, U10 produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Because of this, we think U10's underlying earnings potential is as good as, or possibly even better, than the statutory profit makes it seem! And it's also positive that the company showed enough improvement to book a profit this year, after losing money last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. So while earnings quality is important, it's equally important to consider the risks facing U10 at this point in time. data.title: What Evergy (EVRG)'s Raised Earnings Guidance Means For Shareholders
data.description:

  • The combination of higher earnings guidance, a 4% dividend uplift and a potential US$4 billion capital program with Digital Realty indicates that Evergy is focusing on large load growth while committing more cash returns to shareholders.
  • The next step is to examine how Evergy's raised earnings guidance, supported by expanding data center load, could influence the longer term investment narrative.

Evergy Investment Narrative Recap

For Evergy, the core view is that large data center and industrial demand, combined with heavy grid and generation investment, can support steady earnings while keeping regulators focused on customer bill impacts. The raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to US$4.35 to US$4.50 reflects that view. In the near term, the key swing factor remains execution on new large load contracts and the timing of their usage.

The biggest risk remains on the cost and funding side. Evergy plans high capital spending and already has interest coverage flagged as tight, with dividends not well covered by free cash flow. The latest results do not remove that concern, so the balance among growth spending, financing costs and bill affordability stays central for the next phase.

The most relevant update is the letter of intent with Digital Realty for a potential 1.4 GW project and roughly US$4 billion of capital investment. This is directly tied to Evergy’s data-center-led demand thesis and its plan to grow the regulated rate base through 2030 and beyond. The new agreements that add about 110 MW to existing large load contracts point in the same direction.

This opportunity comes with execution and regulatory risk. Building that much capacity requires Evergy to manage construction costs, interest expense and equity issuance while maintaining acceptable returns. At the same time, regulators will monitor customer affordability and reliability. For you as a shareholder, the key question is whether future earnings from those long-term electric service agreements will comfortably offset the additional capital expenditure and funding burden.

Evergy Forecasts and What Needs To Happen

Evergy's narrative projects US$7.3b revenue and US$1.3b earnings by 2029. This lines up with analysts assuming 6.4% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$374m from US$925.8m today.
